Ah! `test\\[bold]text[/bold]` failed.
Wait, `test\\[bold]` means `\` escapes `[`, so it's `test[bold]text[/bold]`.
The `[bold]` is not a tag, but `[/bold]` is a closing tag.
And since there was no open tag, it failed.

Now let's look at `test\\\\[bold]text[/bold]`.
`\\` is an escaped backslash, so it's `\`.
Then `\\[bold]` is an escaped `[`, so it's `[bold]`.
Wait, `test\\\\[bold]` is `test` + `\\` + `\[bold]`.
`\\` -> `\`
`\[bold]` -> `[bold]`
So it's `test\[bold]text[/bold]`.
Still no open tag.

Wait, I wanted to test `test\\` + `[bold]`.
That would be `test\\[bold]`.
Wait, in Python string literal, `\\` is one backslash.
So `console.print("test\\[bold]text[/bold]")` is actually `test\[bold]text[/bold]`.
The `\` escapes the `[`, so it's `test[bold]text[/bold]`.

If I want `test` + `\` + `[bold]`, I need `test\\` + `[bold]`.
In Python string literal, that's `"test\\[bold]text[/bold]"`.
Wait, I just did that.

Let's use raw strings.

The first `\` escapes the second `\`, so we have `test\` + `[bold]text[/bold]`.
